headline: Asteroids learns to shoot
lede: The small saucer now arrives wild and gets smarter the longer it lives — spray at ±0.55 rad as a rookie, tightening monotonically to the verbatim ±0.15 arcade floor over ten seconds of survival, same dice per shot as before. Leave one alive and its shots go pinpoint: fast kills are the winning law, exactly as on the 1979 cabinet.

notes.text: #3553 shipped at 85f3b61 — SAUCER_AIM learning curve in the sim, replay-deterministic, verified in the live production bundle (token start:1.1,floor:.3,learn:600).
Slot a shipped beside it: ADVENTURE exact sprite-box seam admission (#3552) and two-player hot-seat DEFENDER — a healthy day for the shelf.

Two driver mutants survived the first mutant pass once rookie spray eased early pressure; the fast wave floor was honestly re-pinned to the full sweep's own 40/40 law with numbers measured — then the full 29-mutant suite was run twice at the head in two isolated worktrees: 29/29 both times, plus clean 143/0 and clean fast 113/0.

The four-hands hour: both halves of two lanes crossed the same issue and the same /tmp filenames. New house rules filed into STATE: slot-stamp your log paths, prefer periodic status peeks to hour-long gh watchers (one shared API budget), and check twice before declaring another lane dead.
